svg.text: RESERVE BANK OF INDIA: MONETARY POLICY TOOLS & TRANSMISSION
Quantitative & Qualitative Instruments, Key Policy Rates & Inflation Control (Flexible Target 4% ± 2%)

g.text: QUANTITATIVE / GENERAL INSTRUMENTS
1. Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF):
• REPO RATE: Rate at which RBI lends short-term money to commercial banks against government securities (Policy Rate).
• STANDING DEPOSIT FACILITY (SDF): Introduced 2022; tool to absorb excess liquidity without collateral requirement.
• MARGINAL STANDING FACILITY (MSF): Penal overnight borrowing rate for banks dipping into SLR quota.
2. Reserve Requirements:
• CASH RESERVE RATIO (CRR): Percentage of Net Demand & Time Liabilities (NDTL) banks MUST park in CASH with RBI (no interest earned).
• STATUTORY LIQUIDITY RATIO (SLR): Percentage of NDTL banks MUST maintain in liquid assets (Gold, G-Secs, Cash) with THEMSELVES.
3. Open Market Operations (OMO):
RBI buys/sells G-Secs directly: Selling G-Secs absorbs cash (deflationary); Buying G-Secs injects liquidity (expansionary).
QUALITATIVE / SELECTIVE INSTRUMENTS
1. Margin Requirements (LTV Ratio):
• Proportion of loan value borrower must fund from own equity.
• Raising margin reduces credit flow to speculative sectors.
2. Moral Suasion:
• Informal directives, persuasion and periodic conferences
by RBI Governor to adhere to credit guidelines.
3. Credit Rationing & Priority Sector Lending (PSL):
• Mandatory target: 40% of Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC)
must go to Agriculture, MSMEs, Education, Housing, Weaker Sections.
MONETARY POLICY COMMITTEE (MPC) — STATUTORY SETUP (RBI ACT S. 45ZB):
6 Members: 3 from RBI (Governor as Ex-officio Chair with casting vote) + 3 external experts appointed by Central Govt. Target: CPI Inflation 4% with tolerance band of ± 2% (2% to 6%).
